trial_court: HIGH COURT OF CHHATTISGARH, BILASPUR, F.A.(M) No. 43 of 2007
case_name: Ajay Kumar (Died) Through Lrs Smt.Kusum ... vs Smt. Saraswati Devi & Anr

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Smt. Kusum, W/o Late Shri Ajay Kumar, and her two children Kumari Anchal and Kumari Ritu
parties.respondent_defendant: 1. Smt. Saraswati Devi, W/o Ajay Kumar; 2. Managing Director, Bhilai Steel Plant

facts_of_case: Saraswati Devi filed a suit for declaration that she is the legally wedded wife of Ajay Kumar. She also prayed for a permanent injunction. The trial court held that the marriage between Saraswati Devi and Ajay Kumar was proved and decreed the suit.

legal_principles.principle: The Family Court may receive as evidence any report, statement, documents, information or matter that may assist it to deal effectually with a dispute.
legal_principles.held: Section 14 clearly lays down that the Family Court may receive as evidence, any report, statement, documents, information or matter that may help it to deal with the matter in dispute even if the same is not admissible under the Indian Evidence Act.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party denying a marriage to prove that it is not valid.
legal_principles.held: Ajay Kumar cannot claim that since this is a void marriage he is not bound by the same.

legal_principles.principle: The law is well settled that when there is a relationship, the Court will not permit technicalities to defeat the ends of justice.
legal_principles.held: No doubt the principles of Evidence Act cannot be thrown to the winds but technicalities of the Evidence Act cannot be used to throw out evidence by the Family Court.

outcome.final_order: The final court order declared Saraswati Devi to be the legally wedded wife of Ajay Kumar.
